title: Developer SDKs Integration Garden: Recipes, Canary Scaffolds, and Triage Templates
author: Asha Patel
body:
Overview:
This document is a compact, opinionated catalog of lightweight SDK integration recipes, canary scaffolds, and canonical triage templates designed for product teams and platform integrators. The goal is to accelerate developer onboarding and reduce friction when integrating Redwood Inference SDKs into customer and internal applications while standardizing observability and failure modes.

Intended audience:
- SDK integrators (engineers embedding client libraries)
- Platform and solutions engineers building adapters or third-party connectors
- Support engineers handling integration-level issues

What the Integration Garden contains:
- Small, runnable integration recipes (language + runtime) that exercise common flows: authentication, streaming generation, embeddings, and retries
- Canary scaffolds for incremental rollout: lightweight infra + traffic shaping + telemetry assertions
- Telemetry & contract checklist: required spans, metrics, and event tags for each recipe
- Canonical triage templates and a postmortem checklist for reproducible support handoffs

How to use this page:
1) Choose the recipe matching your client language and pattern (embed, generate, streaming).
2) Wire the telemetry shim described in the Telemetry & Contract Checklist.
3) Launch the canary scaffold against a staging project and run the acceptance probes.
4) Follow the Canary Rollout steps to escalate to production.

Recipes included (high level):
- Node.js streaming adapter: shows incremental parsing of chunked responses and reconnect semantics
- Python embedding batcher: local prefix caching + backpressure example for batched embed calls
- Go server-side generator: request shaper with circuit-breaker and model-variant fallback
- Java client in microservice: token accounting and deterministic retry policy

Telemetry & Contract Checklist (required for every integration)
- Traces:
  - root span: "integration.<service>.request" with tags: sdk.version, model.name, route, tenant.id
  - child span for network layer and KV-cache lookup
- Metrics:
  - counter: sdk.requests_total{status,route,model} (1m, 5m)
  - histogram: sdk.latency_ms_bucket{route} with 50/95/99 quantiles stored
  - gauge: sdk.kv_cache_hit_rate
- Logs/events:
  - Structured logs with request_id, operation, and a compact error_code
- Golden assertions (canary): 95th percentile latency < configured SLO and embedding cosine similarity <= baseline delta

Canary scaffold: checklist and example steps
1) Create a staging environment with the canary scaffold repo (see repo link in related pages).
2) Configure traffic slice: start with 0.5% of non-sensitive traffic or synthetic traffic driven by the contract harness.
3) Wire telemetry: enable sampling=100% for canary traces, route to observability dashboard with the canary tag.
4) Acceptance probes (automated):
   a) Latency probe: 5k synthetic requests, compute P95 over 5m windows
   b) Quality probe: run 100 golden prompts; compute BLEU/ROUGE or embedding similarity as appropriate
   c) Error budget probe: confirm failed request rate < 0.1% over 15m
5) Human review gate: product owner or SRE must sign-off before expanding traffic to 10%.
6) Gradual expansion: 10% -> 50% -> 100% with 30m hold windows and rollback triggers specified below.

Rollback triggers (automated):
- Latency P95 exceeds target by > 2x for two consecutive windows
- Error rate spike > 5x baseline sustained for 10 minutes
- Quality regression: embed similarity drop > configured threshold or average generation score drop > 10%

Canonical triage template (support-ready)
- Title: concise one-line summary
- Impact: number of customers or percentage of traffic affected
- Timeline: first-observed timestamp (UTC) and last-checked timestamp
- Environment: SDK language/version, runtime (node/python/go), deployment zone, model pinned version
- Steps to reproduce: minimal reproducible snippet (use the recipe most similar to customer integration)
- Observed telemetry: key spans, P95 latency, recent error codes, relevant logs (structured JSON snippets)
- Hypothesis: short bullet list of top 3 suspected causes
- Mitigation attempted: list actions (e.g., switch to model-variant X, increase instance count, disable batching)
- Next actions and owner: who will run the deeper investigation and ETA

Example minimal reproducible snippet (Python embedding batcher):
```
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key="${REDWOOD_KEY}")
inputs = ["short text 1", "short text 2"]
resp = client.embeddings.create(model="embed-medium-v1", inputs=inputs, batch_size=8)
print(resp)
```

Configuration reference table (recommended defaults)
| Setting | Recommended default | Notes |
|---------|--------------------:|------|
| batch_size | 8 | Smaller for low-latency interactive apps, larger for throughput jobs |
| max_concurrency | 32 | Bound to client machine capacity |
| request_timeout_ms | 12000 | Includes network + processing; tune for longer context models |
| telemetry_sample_rate | 1.0 (canary) / 0.1 (prod) | Use 100% for early canaries; reduce in prod to control volume |
| kv_cache_ttl_sec | 300 | Short TTL to avoid stale prompts; increase for predictable prefixes |

Operational playbook snippets
- If a canary fails quality probes:
  1) Pause expansion and mark canary as failed.
  2) Run golden prompt differential to identify prompt/temperature/model drift.
  3) If model variant mismatch suspected, switch to fallback variant and re-run probes.
  4) Notify on-call SRE and product owner with triage template filled out.

Common integration failure patterns and canonical fixes
- Pattern: Streaming partial JSON decode errors
  - Cause: client buffer boundary cutting a JSON object in a chunk
  - Fix: Implement a resilient incremental parser that buffers until a complete JSON token is available; add per-chunk length prefix if using bespoke adapters
- Pattern: High per-token cost for interactive usage
  - Cause: unnecessary full-context re-sends in each request
  - Fix: Enable KV prefix caching or use the runtime's prefix caching API; reduce client-side history window and offload session state server-side when safe
- Pattern: Increased latency after a traffic bump
  - Cause: cold model variant scaling or suboptimal batching parameters
  - Fix: Pre-warm pool, lower max_batch_time_ms, and/or provision burst capacity in Dedicated mode

Template repository layout (recommended)
- /recipes/<language>/<pattern>/README.md  -- quick start and minimal code snippet
- /scaffolds/canary/manifest.yaml -- traffic slice, probes, rollback rules
- /telemetry/contract.yaml -- required spans and metrics mapping to dashboards
- /triage/templates/triage-template.md -- copyable triage checklist for support

Maintenance and ownership
- Owner: SDK Integrations Guild (rotation: two engineers, quarterly)
- Review cadence: every quarter or after any major SDK release; reviewers listed at top of page should be notified via PR when changing canary defaults
- Deprecation policy: recipes older than 18 months must be validated or archived; archival requires a short migration note and a linked replacement if available

Related pages and artifacts:
- SDK starter monorepo and telemetry harness (see related_pages)
- Multi-model orchestration examples for service-side fallbacks (see related_pages)

Appendix: acceptance probe queries (examples)
- P95 latency query (PromQL): histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(sdk_latency_ms_bucket[5m])) by (le))
- Error rate (PromQL): sum(rate(sdk_requests_total{status!~"2.."}[5m])) / sum(rate(sdk_requests_total[5m]))

Contact and escalation
- Primary owner: Asha Patel (SDK Integrations Guild lead)
- On-call SRE: see eng-sre/oncall-roster page
- Support escalation: customer-success/integration-escalation-playbook

- 2026-02-15: Created by Asha Patel

Notes and disclaimers:
This page is a pragmatic toolkit—not a strict policy. Teams should adapt thresholds to their product and customer SLAs. If a customer requires enterprise-grade isolation or custom telemetry retention, coordinate with eng-private-deployments and security-and-compliance teams before executing canaries in production.
